newsitem.title: USA: British Airways offers "pay what you weigh" for charity.
newsitem.headline: British Airways offers "pay what you weigh" for charity.

text.p: British Airways is offering the first 100 customers in line at its Logan Airport terminal on May 9 the chance to "pay what they weigh" for a roundtrip ticket between London and Boston.

"The airfare on British Airways from Boston to London normally runs between $400 and $600. So anyone who weighs less than 400 pounds could save," Janet Prensky, a spokeswoman for the airline, said Monday.
The money collected will benefit the Massachusetts Children's Trust Fund, a charity that funds education and support programmes throughout the state, Prensky said.
"We figured that if the average person weighs 150 pounds, we're looking at donating about $15,000," she said.

Travelers will be weighed on the airline's baggage scales and given a letter on which their weight is recorded. They can use that letter to get a roundtrip economy class ticket on the British Airways flight that leaves Boston at 8:25 a.m.
The early morning flight is a new one to London for the airline that begins on May 10.
"We wanted to have some fun and let people know about our newly added flight to London in a memorable way," British Airways sales director Bill Noonan said.
